title: add cohort stability assertions and flake-detection CI hook
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: CI has been noisy for prompt-set regressions where output instability (non-deterministic variation across sampling seeds/temps/minibatches) causes spurious failures. This PR adds a cohort-level stability assertion and a lightweight flake-detection CI hook that (1) computes per-prompt-cohort stability scores during eval runs, (2) compares stability against a stored baseline, and (3) applies a configurable flake policy to reduce noise while still surfacing real regressions. The feature integrates into the existing eval-harness pipeline and GitHub checks: - New metric: stability_score (0..1) defined as 1 - normalized median token-level divergence across N replayed seeds; lower = less stable. - Cohort rules: thresholds by cohort tag (e.g., "conversational", "qa", "api-sample") can be configured in eval_config.yaml. - CI behavior: failures above the regression threshold fail the eval-check job; when instability is detected but under the 'flake_tolerance' threshold the job marks a warning and triggers an automatic single rerun of the eval job to confirm flakiness before failing. - Baseline handling: artifacts/baselines/stability.json stores historical cohort baselines; the check includes a 'record-baseline' subcommand used during baseline rollouts. - Reporting: GitHub check annotations include per-cohort summary and top-3 most unstable prompts (with anonymized IDs). - Telemetry: emits events to eval-telemetry (stability_score, rerun_count, cohort_id) as artifacts for later dashboards. Changes included: hook implementation, metric computation, CI workflow update, unit/integration tests, docs, and an example prompt-set. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves existing eval pass/fail semantics unless a repo config opts into stability assertions (eval_config.yaml flag: enable_stability_assertions). See docs/eval/ci-hooks.md for usage instructions and samples. Rationale: we saw ~6% of CI eval failures in the last month attributable to non-deterministic output; this reduces developer churn while keeping regression sensitivity for true model quality degradation.
